evidence.source_paper: Vanhoof MJM, van Leeuwen T, Galletta L, Vereecke EE. The forearm and hand musculature of semi-terrestrial rhesus macaques (Macaca mulatta) and arboreal gibbons (fam. Hylobatidae). Part II. Quantitative analysis. J Anat. 2021 Feb;238(2):321-337. doi:10.1111/joa.13314. PMCID PMC7812139, PMID 33011967.
evidence.citation_verified_against: the intake's staged front-matter XML of the same article (tools/science_funnel/data/vanhoof_forearm/PMC7812139_fulltext.xml, sha256 47cc6b836d0a9b44d8a1ab35dba1c91114291f63721c2db44175de001c1ce8f8): authors, title, volume 238, issue 2, fpage 321, lpage 337, year 2020/2021, doi 10.1111/joa.13314, PMCID PMC7812139, PMID 33011967 -- all matched
evidence.fetcher: WebFetch (small fast model over PMC full text) + mcp web_reader full-page read (quote cross-checked verbatim between the two reads)
evidence.quote_rendering_note: Equations (1) and (2) are stacked fractions in the source; both independent full-text readers render the fraction bar inline by concatenation, so 'muscle massmuscle fascicle length∗muscle density' reads mass / (muscle fascicle length * muscle density). The semantic form mass/(FL*rho) is confirmed by both readers' formula paraphrases AND by the numbers: at rho = 0.0011 g/mm3 the landed table's implied-rho median is 1.1004 g/cm3 (a different reading of the equation would not put the table's own implied constant at the paper's stated one).
quotes_verbatim: For the small intrinsic hand muscles we were not able to accurately determine the muscle volume using the submersion method. Therefore, we calculated the muscle density only for the extrinsic muscles of all specimens using Equation (2).
For both gibbons and macaques, the average muscle density is 0.0011 g/mm3 (SD <0.0001 g/mm3), which is almost equal to the density defined for human muscles (0.00106 g/mm3) (Ward and Lieber, 2005).
Therefore, the density value of 0.0011 g/mm3 is used in the calculation of the PCSA for all muscles in this study.
evidence.density_citation_named_by_the_paper: Ward S.R. & Lieber R.L. (2005) Density and hydration of fresh and fixed human skeletal muscle. Journal of Biomechanics 38(11):2317-2320 -- the paper's 0.00106 g/mm3 human constant; NOTE: this 1.06 g/cm3 IS the funnel's inherited adapters_muscle.MUSCLE_DENSITY_KG_M3=1060.0 -- the funnel had registered the paper's CITED HUMAN constant, not the paper's own MEASURED-AND-USED macaque/gibbon constant
evidence.pennation_stated_omission: We chose to omit pennation angle (PA ...) from the PCSA equation as (a) there were difficulties in obtaining accurate PA measurements ..., (b) the in vitro measurements are not fully representative of the PA in vivo ..., (c) the PA of most muscles ranges between 0 and 30 degrees, the cosine of which ranges between 1 and 0.87, having only a minor influence on PCSA calculation
evidence.merged_bellies_rule_stated: If muscles consisted of multiple muscle bellies that were easily separable (e.g. m. triceps brachii, m. flexor digitorum superficialis), the PCSA was calculated as the sum of the PCSA of the separate muscle bellies. -- the source's own per-row semantics; per-row residuals on such rows are the source's truth, named not repaired
